messages:
Sam: Small docs ask: can we add a short micro-section in Dedicated provisioning about 'fallback throttling' — i.e., when fallbackModel is rate-limited separately and how that shows up in Console/billing? Getting repeated tickets. CC @indra @kevin

Indra: Good call. We should include a YAML + CLI + one-line billing note. Also a tiny FAQ: how to tell if fallback throttling or reserved exhaustion caused the routing.

Kevin: I'll draft the snippet. Key points: fallbackModel can have separate quota/rate limits and might be subject to tenant-level throttles; fallback_policy.max_fallback_pct should be used to cap impact.

docs-bot: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6012  add fallback throttling micro-section and FAQ.

Kevin: YAML example (concise):
```yaml
provisioning:
  tenant: beta-inc
  reserved_capacity:
    gpus: 2
    model: rdl-large-v1
  scalePolicy:
    target_qps: 80
    cooldown_s: 75
    fallbackModel: rdl-medium-q2
    fallback_policy:
      max_fallback_pct: 20
      fallback_throttle_action: "delay"  # options: delay | drop
  tenant_labels:
    isolation: medium
```

Sam: Nice. Include a short CLI showing how to query fallback throttles in logs.

Indra: CLI (redwoodctl):
```bash
redwoodctl logs query --tenant beta-inc --filter 'routing.variant=fallback OR routing.event=fallback_throttle' --last 30m
```

billing-alfie: Billing note: routed-to-fallback requests count toward tenant usage and are billed at the variant's per-token rate. If fallback is subject to a public quota, customers may see 429s from the fallback endpoint; docs should mention that.

SRE-Jen: Ops troubleshooting steps to add (3 bullets):
- Check ReservedCapacityUtilization in Console; if near 100% reserved, overflow can go to fallback.
- Check redwood_inference_requests_fallback_total metric and compare to fallback quota metrics.
- If you see fallback_throttle events, inspect per-variant quota and consider increasing fallback_policy.max_fallback_pct or disabling fallback temporarily for canary.

Sam: Add a tiny FAQ entry: "My app saw 429s after enabling fallback. Why?" -> "Fallback endpoint can have quotas; if per-variant quota is hit, requests will be throttled (429). The reserved throughput is still guaranteed; throttles are on fallback best-effort path."

Kevin: I'll add a one-liner linking to quota docs and to SLA page (internal). Also make sure to mention cross-region failover can surface similarly if fallback variant differs by region.

Indra: Minor editorial note: use 'fallback' consistently (avoid ‘cheap-variant’ across section). Keep the micro-section under 8 lines.

docs-bot: PR updated with YAML, CLI, FAQ, metrics, and billing note. Reviewers requested: @sam @indra @kevin @billing-alfie @sre-jen

Sam: Thanks — will merge after quick approval. This should cut down the 429 support threads.
